title: Show the DNS servers set for Wi-Fi on macOS
summary: Print the DNS servers that are set for one network service, such as Wi-Fi, using networksetup. You first list your services to get the exact name, then ask for that service's DNS servers.

aliases.text: which dns server is wifi using mac
where to see dns for wifi on mac
dns сервера для wi-fi на маке
какой dns у вайфая на маке

steps.explain: List the network services on this Mac. Find the exact name of the service you want, for example Wi-Fi.
steps.expect: A list of service names, one per line, such as Wi-Fi or Ethernet. A name with * in front is turned off.

steps.explain: Print the DNS servers set for the service. Put the service name from the previous step in double quotes in place of <SERVICE_NAME>.

placeholders.name: SERVICE_NAME
placeholders.description: Network service name exactly as the previous step printed it.

steps.expect: One IP address per line, such as 8.8.8.8. If none were set by hand, a message says no DNS servers are set, and the Mac uses the router's.

source.title: networksetup manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
